land.text: the territory east of Transoxiana that Baraq relinquished to Kaidu in 1267, and the region round Bukhara

predecessors.note: Dated 1267 (Chagatai page) and c.1267/1269 (Kaidu page), before the 1271 investiture.

land.text: Qayaliq southeast of Lake Balkhash, granted to Kaidu by Möngke in 1252
Chapar's territory, surrendered to Duwa in 1306

successors.note: The Kaidu and Duwa pages date the surrender to early 1307.

capitals.name: Qayaliq (Qoylık)
capitals.note: Kaidu was invested with Qayaliq (now Qoylık, southeast of Lake Balkhash) by Möngke in 1252; no page opened names a capital of the ulus, so the one seat the pages name is used. Coordinates approximate.

rulers.name: Kaidu
rulers.note: Invested at Talas in August/September 1271; died late 1301 after the battle south of the Altai.

rulers.name: Chapar
rulers.note: Succeeded Kaidu in 1301 (Kaidu page); the Duwa page has him 'enthroned in 1303'; surrendered to Duwa 1306 (Chagatai page) or early 1307 (Kaidu and Duwa pages).

correction.text: Qayaliq and the lands southeast of Lake Balkhash, the territory east of Transoxiana that Baraq relinquished in 1267, and the region round Bukhara: 'Kaidu also gained control of the region around Bukhara'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The Yuan generals held Almaliq 1266-1276 (war page), so the Ili valley is not drawn yet. The Chagatai khans in the rest of Transoxiana are Kaidu's appointees (vassal events), not Ögedeid land. No infobox area exists; the Chagatai infobox gives 3.4 M km2 for 1310/1350 for the whole western khanate, Ögedeid and Chagatai together.

correction.text: as 1271 plus Almaliq, which Kaidu captured in 1277: 'he was also able to recover control over Almaliq in the east'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Almaliq (Ili valley, Xinjiang) was occupied by Nomukhan's Yuan generals 1266-1276 and fell to Kaidu in 1277. Uighuria stays contested with the Yuan (garrisons at Beshbalik from 1278).

correction.text: as 1277 plus Beshbalik and Uighuria (Turfan-Hami), from which the Yuan withdrew about 1288/89: 'Kaidu and Duwa were able to take over Beshbaliq in 1286, forcing Kublai's troops to evacuate Uighuria and the Tarim Basin over the following years'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Kaidu page dates the takeover of Beshbaliq to 1286, the war page has the Yuan begin to withdraw in 1288/89; 1289 is used. The Tarim Basin is NOT drawn: the pages say the Yuan left it but not who took it, and it is Duwa's Chagatai Khanate in the Cliopatria 1294 shape (see chagatai-khanate). Beshbalik and Turfan-Hami were taken jointly with Duwa.

region.text: Qayaliq southeast of Lake Balkhash, the territory east of Transoxiana and the region round Bukhara

ledger.note: 1271: Kaidu is invested ruler of the Ulus of Ögedei at Talas. 'invested as ruler of the previously dispersed Ulus of Ögedei at a kurultai at Talas in August/September 1271'; Möngke had given him Qayaliq in 1252, Baraq relinquished the territory east of Transoxiana in 1267 (Chagatai page) and Kaidu 'gained control of the region around Bukhara'. The page names no boundary.

region.text: the rest of Transoxiana, ruled by the Chagatai khans Kaidu appointed

ledger.note: 1271: Kaidu sets up the Chagatai khans. After Baraq's death 'Kaidu also appointed Negübei as khan of Chagatai' (Kaidu page); Negübei was killed and replaced by Buqa Temür in 1274 and Kaidu appointed Duwa in 1282 ('In 1282, Kaidu appointed Duwa as head of the Chagatai Khanate', Duwa page): the Chagatai ulus is drawn as Kaidu's client while Kaidu lives.

1275: Kaidu invades Ürümqi. 'He invaded Ürümqi in 1275 and demanded its submission, but the Buddhist Idiqut resisted' and Kublai sent a relief force; the page does not say ground was taken, so this opens the Uighuria front, which the Yuan garrisoned at Beshbalik from 1278.

1277: Kaidu captures Almaliq. The war page: Nomukhan's Yuan generals occupied Almaliq 1266-1276 to block Kaidu, who 'captured Almaliq' in 1277 (Kaidu page: 'he was also able to recover control over Almaliq in the east'). [Reviewer ia-02-x, 2026-10-19] Confidence 3 to 2: neither page dates the capture (Kaidu-Kublai war page: Yuan occupation of Almaliq 1266-1276, then "However, Kaidu captured Almaliq", undated; Kaidu page undated).

1289: the Yuan give up Uighuria. 'The Yuan begin withdrawing from Kashgar, Khotan, and Beshbalik' in 1288/89 (war page); the Kaidu page has Kaidu and Duwa take Beshbaliq in 1286 'forcing Kublai's troops to evacuate Uighuria and the Tarim Basin over the following years'. De facto end year.

1289: Beshbalik and Uighuria pass to Kaidu and Duwa. Kaidu page: 'Kaidu and Duwa were able to take over Beshbaliq in 1286, forcing Kublai's troops to evacuate Uighuria and the Tarim Basin over the following years'; 1289 is the withdrawal year of the war page. Shared with Duwa's Chagatai ulus; the Tarim Basin is not credited to Kaidu here.

1289: Kaidu takes Karakorum. 'defeating Kublai's grandson Kammala and capturing the old capital Karakorum in 1289'; he retreated when Kublai advanced (the war page mentions only the 1301 attack on Karakorum).
1289: Kaidu leaves Karakorum when Kublai advances; the Kaidu page gives the capture in 1289 and the retreat in the same campaign, the exact month is not given.

region.text: the Altai and western Mongolia between Karakorum and the Dzungarian steppe

ledger.note: 1289: the war moves to the Altai and western Mongolia. After Karakorum (1289) the fighting ran to the Altai: Kaidu defeated Khayishan in 1300 and was beaten south of the Altai in 1301. The zone is the researcher's reading of 'west of the Altai' and Karakorum.

1301: Kaidu dies after the last battle. 'Kaidu and Duwa attack Karakorum. Neither side wins decisively, Duwa is wounded, and Kaidu dies soon after' (war page); Temür made peace with the western khanates c.1304 (Duwa page) and Duwa and Chapar recognized Yuan authority in 1303 (Chagatai page).

1306: Duwa throws off Chapar's overlordship. 'Duwa threw off his allegiance to Chapar' (Chagatai page); Chapar 'fell out with Duwa by 1306' (Kaidu page). The Chagatai ulus ceases to be the Ögedeid client.

1306: Chapar surrenders his lands to Duwa. 'forcing him to surrender his territory to Duwa in 1306' (Chagatai page); the Kaidu and Duwa pages put the surrender in early 1307 and Yuan troops came to help Duwa. The page names no places, so the region is the last keyframe.
1306: the Ögedeid ulus ends. Chapar gives up his realm to Duwa; Yangichar replaced Chapar and 'Yangichar and Chapar both submitting to Qayishan... in 1310' (Kaidu page).

wars.name: Kaidu–Kublai war
wars.outcome: Inconclusive (infobox): Kaidu held Almaliq from 1277 and Beshbalik and Uighuria from the late 1280s; the Yuan held Mongolia. Duwa and Chapar recognized Yuan authority in 1303 and a general peace followed c.1304.
wars.note: The war page's infobox lists Chagatai Khanate and House of Ögedei against the Yuan (1271-1301), the Golden Horde with Kaidu until 1284.

wars.name: Ilkhanate–Ögedeid raids on Khorasan
wars.outcome: Raids and rebel support in Khorasan; no border change recorded. 'By 1288, however, Kaidu was at war with the Ilkhan, raiding into Khurasan'; his son Sarban invaded Khurasan in 1302.
wars.note: The war page says Kaidu's forces 'occupy Ilkhanid Khorasan' in the early 1290s; no page dates an end, so no occupation event is recorded (the ilkhanate dossier owns the Khorasan side).

wars.name: Duwa–Chapar war
wars.outcome: Duwa defeated Chapar's supporter Baba; Chapar surrendered after Yuan forces came to help Duwa. Duwa received gifts from Temür; Duwa died in 1307.
wars.note: The Duwa page: 'Around 1305 or 1306' Duwa tried to take parts of the lands Temür had granted Chapar.

certainty.note: Steppe and Tarim-edge frontiers throughout; no treaty line is recorded.

sources.title: Kaidu
sources.note: Kaidu: 1252 Qayaliq, 1271 Talas kurultai (Ulus of Ogedei), Bukhara region, 1286 Beshbaliq, 1289 Karakorum, 1301 death, Chapar to 1307, 1310 submission.

sources.title: Chagatai Khanate
sources.note: Chagatai ulus 1227-1294: 1267 Baraq relinquishes the east, 1272 Abaqa sacks Bukhara, 1306 Chapar surrenders territory to Duwa; infobox area 3.4 M km2.

sources.title: Kaidu–Kublai war
sources.note: Kaidu-Kublai war 1268-1301: Almaliq 1277, Ürümqi 1275, Yuan garrisons and withdrawal 1288/89, Khorasan, 1301 Karakorum.

sources.title: Duwa
sources.note: Duwa: appointed by Kaidu in 1282; Chapar enthroned 1303; fighting with Chapar c.1305-06; surrender, 1307.

sources.title: House of Ögedei
sources.note: House of Ogedei: family page; 1310 Chapar submits to Khayishan; thin on territory.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for the Ogedeid ulus; Cliopatria's Chagatai Khanate row (from 1294) must be read together with this dossier: Kaidu held Semirechye, Almaliq, Bukhara and (with Duwa) Beshbalik/Uighuria, while Duwa held the rest of Transoxiana as Kaidu's appointee until 1306. The pages do not divide the Tarim Basin between Kaidu and Duwa after the Yuan left (1288/89); it is left to chagatai-khanate.

Pages that disagree: Ogedei's ulus end 1306 (Chagatai page) vs early 1307 (Kaidu and Duwa pages); Beshbaliq taken 1286 (Kaidu page) vs Yuan withdrawing 1288/89 (war page); Karakorum captured 1289 (Kaidu page) vs only the 1301 attack (war page). Chapar succeeded 1301 (Kaidu page) or was enthroned 1303 (Duwa page). The en.wikipedia article 'Ögedei Khanate' did not load (URL not found, three spellings); 'House of Ögedei' is a family page. No capital is named by any page: Qayaliq is Kaidu's 1252 appanage and is used as the seat.

Counterparts that need entries in other dossiers: yuan-dynasty (Almaliq occupied by Nomukhan 1266-1276; Beshbalik garrison 1278; Yuan withdrawal 1288/89; Chapar recognizes Yuan authority 1303, Yangichar and Chapar submit 1310); ulus-of-chagatai (1267 loss of the east; Kaidu's appointees); ilkhanate (Khorasan raids from 1288/90s); golden-horde (Mongke-Temur allied with Kaidu until 1284). Region names all resolve in the gazetteer; 'Qayaliq' is not a place name there (Taldyqorghan used).
